requirements.text: The warehouse must record every vendor, being a company from which goods are purchased.
A vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number, the number by which purchasing staff and vendor correspondence refer to the company.
The warehouse must retain the internal business entity identifier of each vendor in addition to the vendor account number, because other purchasing records point to the internal identifier.
The warehouse must record the vendor's company name and make it reportable.
Each vendor carries a credit rating on a five-point scale: Superior, Excellent, Above average, Average, Below average.
Reporting must present the vendor credit rating in its business wording, not as a bare code.
Each vendor carries a preferred vendor status that is either 'preferred over other vendors supplying the same product' or 'do not use if another vendor is available'.
Purchasing management must be able to see whether purchase orders are actually being placed with preferred vendors.
requirements.obj: purchase orders placed with preferred vendors

requirements.text: Each vendor carries an active flag indicating whether the vendor is still actively used or is no longer used.
Vendors that are no longer used must remain in the warehouse so that historical orders placed with them stay reportable.
Where a vendor offers an electronic purchasing interface, the warehouse must record the purchasing web service address.
The purchasing web service address is not always populated, and reporting must tolerate its absence.
The warehouse must retain the history of changes to vendor attributes, in particular credit rating, preferred status and active flag.
The state of a vendor at the time an order was placed must be reconstructable, not only its current state.
The warehouse must record, for each combination of a product and a vendor, the standing commercial terms under which the product is bought from that vendor.
The same product may be supplied by several vendors, and a vendor may supply several products.
A supply relationship is identified in business terms by the pairing of the product and the vendor.
The warehouse must record the average lead time, in days, between placing an order with the vendor and receiving the purchased product, as an input to purchasing planning and supplier comparison.
The warehouse must record the standard price, the vendor's usual selling price for the product.
The warehouse must record the last receipt cost, the selling price when the product was last purchased from the vendor.
The warehouse must record the last receipt date, the date the product was last received from the vendor, so the business can see price drift between agreed and actually paid price.
The warehouse must record the agreed minimum and maximum order quantities for the product from the vendor, so buyers and reporting can see whether orders respect the agreed bounds.

The meanings of the minimum and maximum order quantity fields are transposed in the source descriptions and must be confirmed with the purchasing team before either is used in reporting or threshold checks.
The quantity currently on order for the product from the vendor must be available as an indicator of open commitment.
The warehouse must record the unit of measure in which the product is bought from the vendor.

Quantities and prices must always be interpreted together with the unit of measure of the vendor-product supply relationship, since the same product may be bought in different units from different vendors.
The warehouse must retain the history of supply terms (price, lead time, quantity bounds) so that trends in agreed price and lead time per vendor and product can be analysed.
Quantity on order and last receipt figures are running values updated as activity occurs, and reporting must be clear about whether it shows the current value or the value as at a point in time.
The warehouse must be able to identify each purchased product consistently and join purchasing activity to product information maintained outside the purchasing area.
The warehouse must record every purchase order placed with a vendor.
A purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number.
Each purchase order is placed with exactly one vendor.
Each purchase order is created by one employee, the buyer who raised it.
The warehouse must be able to report purchasing activity by the employee who created the order.
Each purchase order names a shipping method, being the shipping company and rate agreement used to bring the goods.
Each purchase order carries an order date, the date the order was created.
Each purchase order carries an estimated shipment date, the date the vendor is expected to ship, to be compared against actual receipt activity.
Each purchase order carries a status that is one of Pending, Approved, Rejected or Complete.
Reporting must present purchase order status in business wording.
The business must be able to see the population of orders in each status, in particular orders that are approved but not yet complete.
Each purchase order carries a revision number, an incrementing counter tracking how the order has changed.
The business must be able to know whether an order was revised and how many times.
The warehouse must retain the history of a purchase order as it changes, with status transitions and revisions traceable over time rather than overwritten by the latest state.
The business must be able to answer when an order was approved and how long it sat pending.
requirements.obj: order approval time and pending duration

requirements.text: Each purchase order carries financial totals: a subtotal (sum of the value of its lines), a tax amount, a freight amount, and a total due to the vendor (subtotal plus tax plus freight).
The business must be able to analyse purchasing spend by vendor, by employee, by shipping method and over time using order totals.
The warehouse must be able to demonstrate that reported order totals are consistent with the underlying order lines.
Any discrepancy between the stated order total and the sum of its lines must be surfaced as a finding.
Freight and tax are order-level charges and are not attributed to individual products in the source.
If product-level landed cost is wanted, the basis for allocating freight and tax across lines must be decided by the business, as it cannot be derived from the source.
Each purchase order contains one or more lines, one per purchased product.
A purchase order line is identified in business terms by its purchase order together with its line number.
Each purchase order line refers to exactly one product.
Each line carries the quantity ordered.
Each line carries the unit price, the vendor's selling price for a single unit of the product on this order.
Each line carries a line total equal to the ordered quantity multiplied by the unit price.
Each line carries a due date on which the product is expected to be received, held per line so that different products on one order may be expected at different times.
Delivery-performance analysis must work at line level, not only at order level.
The business must be able to compare the unit price actually paid on a line with the standard price agreed for that product and vendor to identify off-contract purchasing.
requirements.obj: line unit price against standard price

requirements.text: Each purchase order line must record the quantity actually received from the vendor.
Each line must record the quantity rejected during inspection.
Each line must record the quantity accepted into inventory, being the received quantity less the rejected quantity.
The business must be able to measure the fulfilment gap between ordered and received quantity, including under-delivery and over-delivery, per line, per order, per product and per vendor.
The business must be able to measure inspection reject rates, being rejected quantity as a share of received quantity, by vendor and by product as the primary indicator of incoming quality.
The warehouse must retain the progression of received and rejected quantities per line so that the quantity received as at a given date can be answered and partial deliveries are visible.

The source records only cumulative received, rejected and accepted quantities per line with a last-updated date, and does not record individual receipt events, receipt dates or per-delivery inspection outcomes; analysis of individual deliveries requires another source or dropping the requirement.
The business must be able to compare the due date on a line against evidence of actual receipt to measure on-time delivery by vendor.

The only available measure of actual receipt timing is the last receipt date on the vendor-product supply relationship, and its sufficiency as a basis for an on-time-delivery metric must be agreed with the business.
The business must be able to compare actual elapsed time from order to receipt against the average lead time recorded for the vendor and product to validate whether recorded lead times are realistic.
requirements.obj: actual elapsed time against average lead time

requirements.text: The warehouse must record every shipping method available for inbound purchases.
A shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name.
The warehouse must also retain the internal shipping method identifier used on purchase orders.
Each shipping method carries a minimum shipping charge (ship base) and a charge per pound (ship rate), the terms on which freight is expected to be charged.
The business must be able to analyse freight cost by shipping method.
The business must be able to compare freight actually charged on orders against the base and per-pound rates agreed with the shipping company.
requirements.obj: freight charged against agreed shipping rates

requirements.text: The warehouse must retain the history of ship base and ship rate so freight charged on a historical order can be assessed against the rates in force at that time.
The technical replication identifier on shipping method records carries no business meaning and is not required for reporting.
Products bought on order lines are normally, but not necessarily, products with a recorded supply relationship with that vendor.
Where an order line names a product with no recorded supply relationship for that vendor, this must be surfaced as a finding rather than hidden as a data error.
The warehouse must use the last-modified date and time carried by every purchasing source record to establish when information changed.
The warehouse must not present a value as current when a more recent change exists.

All monetary amounts in the purchasing source are held in a single currency with no currency indicator, and if vendors are paid in other currencies the currency of orders and prices must be clarified because it cannot be established from the schema.
Codes with defined business meanings (purchase order status, vendor credit rating, preferred vendor status, active flag) must be presented in reporting in their business wording.
The mapping of codes to business wording must be held once and applied consistently.
Aggregating quantities across products or units of measure without regard to the unit must be prevented in reporting.
requirements.obj: aggregation of quantities across units of measure

requirements.text: Records that no longer represent current operational reality, such as inactive vendors, completed or rejected orders and discontinued supply relationships, must be retained in full.
Nothing may be physically removed from the warehouse because it has ceased to be current.

business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 explicitly states a vendor is identified in business terms by its vendor account number, used by purchasing staff and in correspondence; it is business-recognised, unique and stable (Vendor.AccountNumber).

REQ-003 requires retaining it because other purchasing records (e.g. PurchaseOrderHeader.VendorID, ProductVendor.BusinessEntityID) reference it; it is an internal/system identifier, so weaker than the account number but needed as a technical reference.
REQ-031 states a purchase order is identified in business terms by its purchase order number; unique, stable and non-null, and referenced by order lines.

business_keys.field: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID (purchase order with line number)
business_keys.rationale: REQ-052 states a line is identified by its purchase order together with its line number; the composite is unique and stable (REQ-051).
REQ-017 states a supply relationship is identified by the pairing of the product and the vendor (REQ-015, REQ-016: many-to-many), matching ProductVendor's ProductID and BusinessEntityID.
REQ-071 states a shipping method is identified in business terms by the shipping company name (ShipMethod.Name); business-recognised and unique.
REQ-072 requires retaining the internal identifier used on purchase orders (REQ-035) for referencing; it is system-generated so a weak business key compared to the name.

REQ-029 requires consistent identification of purchased products and joining to product information maintained outside purchasing; ProductID appears on order lines (REQ-053) and supply relationships. Requirements do not explicitly call it unique, so confidence is moderate.

REQ-033 and REQ-034 state each purchase order is created by one employee (PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID) and reporting is by employee; the requirements name no other identifier, so this is the only available key and may be an internal ID.

satellites.description: Order-level financial totals: subtotal, tax, freight and total due.
satellites.split_rationale: Monetary amounts grouped together for spend analysis and reconciliation against lines.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_terms
satellites.description: Ordered quantity, unit price, line total and due date of the line.
satellites.split_rationale: Order terms set when the line is placed, changing rarely.

satellites.name: sat_purchase_order_line_receipt
satellites.description: Cumulative received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities, historised to show receipt progression.
satellites.split_rationale: Running receipt figures that change with deliveries, split from the static order terms; carries ModifiedDate.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_terms
satellites.description: Standing commercial supply terms: average lead time, standard price, min/max order quantities.
satellites.split_rationale: Agreed terms changing slowly, historised for trend analysis; separated from running values.

satellites.name: sat_product_vendor_running_values
satellites.description: Running values updated with activity: last receipt cost and date, quantity on order.
satellites.split_rationale: Fast-changing activity-driven figures, split from agreed terms by rate of change; carries ModifiedDate.

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_rates
satellites.description: Ship base and ship rate, historised so historical freight can be assessed against rates in force.
satellites.split_rationale: Changing rate terms; rowguid excluded as it has no business meaning (REQ-077).

satellites.name: sat_ship_method_identifiers
satellites.description: Internal shipping method identifier used on purchase orders.
satellites.split_rationale: Static internal identifier, separated from changing rates.

schema.name: ModifiedDate

schema.name: Freight

schema.name: ModifiedDate

# ADR-0001: Data Vault model derived from requirements

**Status:** Proposed
**Date:** 2026-11-15
**Decision makers:** Vault-Agent (generated) — pending human review

## Context

This model was derived automatically by the Vault-Agent pipeline from 87 requirement(s) and 9 business key candidate(s). It records the Data Vault 2.0 structures the modeler chose and traces each back to the requirements that justify it.

## Decision

Model the following Data Vault 2.0 structures.

### Hubs (3)

- **hub_purchase_order** — business key `PurchaseOrderID`. A purchase order placed with a vendor, identified by its purchase order number. _(requirements: REQ-030, REQ-031, REQ-086)_
- **hub_purchase_order_line** — business key `purchase_order_line`. A line of a purchase order, identified by the purchase order together with its line number. _(requirements: REQ-051, REQ-052, REQ-058)_
- **hub_ship_method** — business key `Name`. A shipping method (shipping company and rate agreement) for inbound purchases, identified by the shipping company name. _(requirements: REQ-070, REQ-071, REQ-035)_

### Links (5)

- **link_purchase_order_business_entity_ship_method** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity (vendor), hub_business_entity (employee), hub_ship_method. Purchase order header relationships: the order is placed with exactly one vendor, created by one employee (buyer) and names one shipping method. Built from PurchaseOrderHeader (VendorID, EmployeeID, ShipMethodID). Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID with its VendorID, EmployeeID and ShipMethodID as recorded on the order header. _(requirements: REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-035, REQ-046, REQ-008, REQ-074)_
- **link_purchase_order_line** — connects hub_purchase_order_line, hub_purchase_order, hub_product. A purchase order line belongs to its purchase order and refers to exactly one product (joined to the existing product hub via ProductID). Unit of work: PurchaseOrderID + PurchaseOrderDetailID with the ProductID ordered on that line. _(requirements: REQ-051, REQ-053, REQ-029, REQ-063, REQ-064, REQ-078)_
- **link_product_vendor** — connects hub_product, hub_business_entity (vendor), hub_unit_measure. Vendor-product supply relationship (many-to-many) from ProductVendor, including the unit of measure in which the product is bought from that vendor. Unit of work: ProductID + BusinessEntityID (vendor) pairing with its UnitMeasureCode. _(requirements: REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-025, REQ-026, REQ-029, REQ-079)_
- **link_purchase_order_line_product** — connects hub_purchase_order_line, hub_product. Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderDetail.ProductID references PRODUCTNUMBER; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34). _(requirements: —)_
- **link_purchase_order_business_entity** — connects hub_purchase_order, hub_business_entity. Declared foreign key PurchaseOrderHeader.EmployeeID references BUSINESSENTITYID; ratified from the source catalogue (WP34). _(requirements: —)_

### Satellites (11)

- **sat_business_entity_vendor_details** — on hub_business_entity; payload: AccountNumber, Name, PurchasingWebServiceURL. Vendor identification and descriptive details: account number, company name, optional purchasing web service address. Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Slow-changing identifying/descriptive vendor attributes, separated from the status codes whose history is analysed.. _(requirements: REQ-002, REQ-004, REQ-011, REQ-012)_
- **sat_business_entity_vendor_status** — on hub_business_entity; payload: CreditRating, PreferredVendorStatus, ActiveFlag, ModifiedDate. Vendor classification codes with history: credit rating, preferred status, active flag. Source table: Vendor. Split rationale: Coded status attributes whose change history must be retained and reconstructed at order time; carries the record's ModifiedDate.. _(requirements: REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-080, REQ-083)_
- **sat_purchase_order_status** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: Status, RevisionNumber, ModifiedDate. Purchase order status and revision number, historised to trace status transitions and revisions. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Fast-changing workflow state, kept apart from dates and financial totals.. _(requirements: REQ-038, REQ-039, REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-080)_
- **sat_purchase_order_dates** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: OrderDate, ShipDate. Order date and estimated shipment date of the purchase order. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Scheduling dates, largely static once set.. _(requirements: REQ-036, REQ-037)_
- **sat_purchase_order_totals** — on hub_purchase_order; payload: SubTotal, TaxAmt, Freight, TotalDue. Order-level financial totals: subtotal, tax, freight and total due. Source table: PurchaseOrderHeader. Split rationale: Monetary amounts grouped together for spend analysis and reconciliation against lines.. _(requirements: REQ-045, REQ-046, REQ-047, REQ-048, REQ-049, REQ-075, REQ-082)_
- **sat_purchase_order_line_terms** — on hub_purchase_order_line; payload: OrderQty, UnitPrice, LineTotal, DueDate. Ordered quantity, unit price, line total and due date of the line. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Order terms set when the line is placed, changing rarely.. _(requirements: REQ-054, REQ-055, REQ-056, REQ-057, REQ-059, REQ-067)_
- **sat_purchase_order_line_receipt** — on hub_purchase_order_line; payload: ReceivedQty, RejectedQty, StockedQty, ModifiedDate. Cumulative received, rejected and accepted (stocked) quantities, historised to show receipt progression. Source table: PurchaseOrderDetail. Split rationale: Running receipt figures that change with deliveries, split from the static order terms; carries ModifiedDate.. _(requirements: REQ-060, REQ-061, REQ-062, REQ-063, REQ-064, REQ-065, REQ-066, REQ-080)_
- **sat_product_vendor_terms** — on link_product_vendor; payload: AverageLeadTime, StandardPrice, MinOrderQty, MaxOrderQty. Standing commercial supply terms: average lead time, standard price, min/max order quantities. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Agreed terms changing slowly, historised for trend analysis; separated from running values.. _(requirements: REQ-018, REQ-019, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-027, REQ-069)_
- **sat_product_vendor_running_values** — on link_product_vendor; payload: LastReceiptCost, LastReceiptDate, OnOrderQty, ModifiedDate. Running values updated with activity: last receipt cost and date, quantity on order. Source table: ProductVendor. Split rationale: Fast-changing activity-driven figures, split from agreed terms by rate of change; carries ModifiedDate.. _(requirements: REQ-020, REQ-021, REQ-024, REQ-028, REQ-068, REQ-080)_
- **sat_ship_method_rates** — on hub_ship_method; payload: ShipBase, ShipRate, ModifiedDate. Ship base and ship rate, historised so historical freight can be assessed against rates in force. Source table: ShipMethod. Split rationale: Changing rate terms; rowguid excluded as it has no business meaning (REQ-077).. _(requirements: REQ-073, REQ-074, REQ-075, REQ-076, REQ-080)_
- **sat_ship_method_identifiers** — on hub_ship_method; payload: ShipMethodID. Internal shipping method identifier used on purchase orders. Source table: ShipMethod. Split rationale: Static internal identifier, separated from changing rates.. _(requirements: REQ-072)_

### Hub keys decided before modelling (1)

- **ShipMethod** — key `Name`: the declared natural key, taken as the default of a contested case; primary key `ShipMethodID`.

### Source mappings (39)

Where each modelled concept's values come from (ADR-0008). The category is the deterministic confidence tier; `accepted` / `overridden` mark a human decision, `proposed` still awaits one.

- `PurchaseOrderID` → `PurchaseOrderHeader`.`PurchaseOrderID` — exact_name, accepted
- `purchase_order_line` → `PurchaseOrderDetail`.`PurchaseOrderDetailID` — comment_grounded, accepted
- `Name` → `ShipMethod`.`Name` — exact_name, accepted
- `AccountNumber` → `Vendor`.`AccountNumber` — exact_name, accepted
- `Name` → `Vendor`.`Name` — exact_name, accepted
